title: One Pot, 20 Spices, and You Cook Your Own Dinner — Hotpot | China Travel Expert
description:
One boiling pot in the middle of the table — and everyone cooks their own dinner. That's Chinese hotpot.

A shared broth simmers in the center of the table while diners dip in raw meat, seafood and vegetables and fish them back out seconds later — a communal ritual, not a solo meal. The famous Sichuan/Chongqing version is a dark-red broth loaded with around twenty spices, chilies and mouth-numbing Sichuan pepper, and the modern spicy style is often traced to riverside and dock workers in Chongqing who simmered cheap cuts to stay warm. It's peak-season food as the weather cools.

🧭 Expert Tip: If you can't take the heat, ask for a 鸳鸯 (yuanyang) split pot — spicy broth on one side, mild bone or mushroom broth on the other. Nobody has to lose.

一口锅摆在桌子中间，每个人都自己涮自己的那一口。
